questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I always wanted to go to Norway for a longer period of time, and this was the perfect opportunity to do so. Also, in Oslo I had the opportunity to take courses that I would not be able to other places.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, I got emails continuously with information I needed. And I could always contact the exchange coordinator and the faculty also had an information center

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had gotten an e-mail with the place we had to show up at on our first day. And the first day we had tutors showing us around, and our exchange coordinator gave us a lot of information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation week was good information wise, but not that great socially. We got divided in to groups to have a tour around campus, but the groups was way too large, so it was almost impossible to actually talk to people or remember them

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through SiO which is an organisation that the university cooperates with. You just make a wishlist with some of their different accommodations and then hope you get one offered. You are more likely to get housing if you are open for other housing types than the one you wished for.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is super easy to get around in Oslo, so it is no problem to live off campus. Most student accommodations are off campus, and are placed in student villages.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not get the kind of housing I originally wished for, but ended up being really glad about the one that I got

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you find the courses that you wanted in the course catalog, and then you registered for the course on Studentweb using the course 'code', when registration opened. It was possible to register for more courses than what you needed, that way you had more changes to get in to courses that you wanted. Then when you had gotten the answer back, you could drop the ones you did not need.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always contact the faculties for information or the administation

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registrer for more courses than you need at first, that way you have a bigger chance of getting the ones you want, rather than having to reapply if you did not get all the courses that you need. Make sure to check time and place for your courses, so that you have enough time in between classes to get from one place to the other, especially if you have classes on different campuses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One of my courses were for first semesters. so at first it was a lot of information about how to be in academica, but later the classes were great. However I felt like we only scratched the surface on a lot of subjects

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH I normally have a lot more group work, where we work with the material and the theories. We did not do that as much at my host university, which was something I missed

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
KRIM1100 - Inføring i kriminologi
SOS2305 - Avikk, kriminalitet og straff
SOS2550 - The sociologi og subcultures and groups

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the subject SOS2550 - The sociologi og subcultures and groups. It was nice to get a theoretical perspective on something that we all are apart of in our everyday life.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I took a few more trips around Norway that I had originally planed, which also gave more expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was expensive but I new that was most likely

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of stuff was available, but it was not advertised really well

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had a friend who volunteered at one of the student cafés. That sounded like a good thing to do, that way you get to meet new and local people. I had a membership at SiO Athletica, which is a gym, that have great training classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take trips around Norway. Rent a cabin some place, that is a very norwegian thing to do. Use the great nature around and go for walks in the parks or neighborhoods

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. It is quite similar to danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything particularly challenging. However most shops are closed on Sundays which took me some time getting used to

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their relationship to nature, and that they use it a lot. I came to like that the shops are closed on Sundays, so that Sunday was more a day for walks, coffee with friends or for going on museums.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Getting friends from your home country are just as good at getting friends from other countries. 
2. There is no right way to do exchange - dont compare yourself to others experience 
3. Go on trips - with ESN or on your own or with friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I went on exchange with three people from my class, and I had the best time experiencing  everything with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The way that they have exams are quite different than what I am used to, but it was fine

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
